History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden onset shortness of breath that began ≈1 hour ago while the patient was seated watching television.  
• Course: Ongoing; patient uncertain if worsening; feels “stressed” with prominent palpitations.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Dry cough began the day before.  
  – Chest soreness when taking a deep breath; abdominal (C-section) scar also tender.  
• Denies frank chest pain at rest, sputum production, fever, leg pain/swelling.  
• Relevant context: Caesarean section 4 weeks ago; currently caring for 4-week-old infant. Family history significant for mother with leg clots.  

Past Medical History:
• Caesarean section (4 weeks postpartum).  
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
Allergies: Ibuprofen – reaction not recalled (details not documented).  
Medications: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); taken regularly after surgery, last dose ≈1 week ago.  
Other medications/vaccinations: Not recorded.

Physical Examination:
• General: Patient alert, speaking in full sentences via video/phone.  
• Cardiovascular: Self-counted radial pulse 30 beats in 15 s (interpreted as ≈120 bpm) → tachycardia.  
• Respiratory: Reports subjective dyspnea; no wheeze or stridor noted over call.  
• Chest wall/abdomen: Mild chest discomfort on deep inspiration; C-section scar tender to touch (per history).  
• Extremities: No reported leg pain or swelling.  
• Additional vitals (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature) and focused physical findings: Not recorded.

Impression:
Acute postpartum dyspnea with tachycardia – high concern for pulmonary embolism.  
Top differentials consistent with transcript:  
1. Pulmonary embolism – sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, 4 wks post-cesarean (hypercoagulable), family history of DVT.  
2. Acute respiratory infection/early pneumonia – new cough and pleuritic discomfort but lacks fever or gradual progression.  
3. Anxiety/panic episode – stress and palpitations could contribute, but organic risk factors predominate.  
Conflict noted: Date of birth reported as 20 Apr 1980 by patient; clinician repeated 1983.

Management Plan:
• Advised immediate hospital evaluation for suspected pulmonary embolism.  
• Transport: Patient elected self-transport with baby; ambulance offered but declined.  
• Medication guidance: Hold further codeine until reviewed.  
• Education: Explained risk of post-operative/post-partum blood clots in lungs or legs and need for urgent assessment and possible anticoagulation.  
• Safety-netting: If symptoms worsen en route or before leaving (severe chest pain, dizziness, collapse), call emergency services (ambulance) immediately.

Patient Summary:
Four-week postpartum woman developed sudden shortness of breath and tachycardia while at rest. Given recent C-section and family history, pulmonary embolism is the leading concern. She will proceed to the emergency department for definitive evaluation and management.

Key Takeaways:
• Go to the hospital straight away for tests to rule out a blood clot in the lungs.  
• Do not take additional codeine until assessed.  
• Bring essentials for yourself and the baby; call emergency services if symptoms rapidly worsen.

Next Steps:
• Emergency department to obtain full vitals, ECG, D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q scan, and start anticoagulation if PE confirmed.  
• Consider complete blood count, COVID/respiratory viral testing, and chest X-ray if infection suspected.  
• Arrange postpartum follow-up and VTE prophylaxis plan once acute issue addressed.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: Full vital signs, detailed allergy reaction, comprehensive medication list, smoking/alcohol history, obstetric/gynecologic history beyond recent C-section.  
• Conflicts: Patient stated DOB 1980; clinician echoed 1983 (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational repetitions but overall adequate for documentation.
